alignments.note: Article takes the determiner with the dative's case preposition riding along under rule 21.
Substantival adjective, bare behind its own article.
Subjunctive with subject and modal; head on the lexical verb.

The article's complement is a substantival quantifier and no noun is expressed, so the supplied nominal *men* is the article's own under rules 49 and 102, exactly as `οἱ ἡμέτεροι` → *our people* gives *people* to the article; the dative's case preposition rides along as rule 102's `τοῦ κυρίου` → *the kingdom* of has it, and rule 22 heads the unit on the nominal word. Discontinuous around *all* under rule 15.
Substantival quantifier keeps a bare *all*, the supplied nominal having gone to the article that governs it.
Perfect with subject and auxiliary; head on the lexical verb.
Anarthrous substantival quantifier with its generic completion; no article competes, so rule 102's anarthrous clause keeps *things* on the quantifier and rule 17 heads there.
Adverb rendered by the frame *by all means*; head on *all*, the word realizing the παντ- lexeme, rather than on the frame's formal noun (rule 17). Heading on *means* remains defensible.
Subjunctive with subject and modal; head on the lexical verb, discontinuous around the adverbial frame under rule 15.

review_notes: Corrected: `τοῖς` (s009) is `aligned` to *to … men* rather than left `unrepresented`. Rule 21's determinerless clause is for an article governing an expressed noun; here the complement is a substantival quantifier and the ASV supplies the nominal, which rules 49 and 102 make the article's own — `οἱ ἡμέτεροι` → *our people* is the determinerless instance, and rule 102 records the substantival-adjective shape as twelve units to none.
`πᾶσιν` accordingly keeps a bare *all*, matching this chapter's own `τὰ πνευματικά` → *things* / *spiritual* and `τὰ σαρκικά` → *things* / *carnal* at 9:11 (rule 24).
9:19's anarthrous `πάντων` → *all men* is untouched: rule 102 scopes rule 17's generic-noun clause to anarthrous Greek, where no article stands to take the supplied noun.
The head of `πάντως` → *by all means* is contested; the unit's note names the competing reading.
